title.en: A Stop on the Bare Rock
title.fr: Une halte sur la roche nue

summary.en: This place has something to tell you. Stop, read it, then answer three questions about who Canadians are.
summary.fr: Ce lieu a quelque chose à vous apprendre. Arrêtez-vous, lisez, puis répondez à trois questions sur qui sont les Canadiens.

text.en: This place is not going anywhere. Come back whenever you like.
text.fr: Ce lieu ne bouge pas d'ici. Revenez quand vous voudrez.

text.en: There are still three questions here, about who Canadians are.
text.fr: Il reste ici trois questions sur qui sont les Canadiens.

text.en: Across Canada, people of many backgrounds and many faiths live and work peacefully side by side, proud to be Canadians.
text.fr: Partout au Canada, des personnes d'origines et de croyances diverses vivent et travaillent paisiblement côte à côte, fières d'être canadiennes.

source.quote: Many ethnic and religious groups live and work in peace as proud Canadians.

verification.evidence: Many ethnic and religious groups live and work in peace as proud Canadians.

text.en: You walked the bare rock and answered three questions about who Canadians are.
text.fr: Vous avez marché sur la roche nue et répondu à trois questions sur qui sont les Canadiens.

text.en: You have reached the light on the bare rock. Two things about this country come first, then three questions.
text.fr: Vous voici au phare, sur la roche nue. D'abord deux choses sur ce pays, puis trois questions.

text.en: Canada has two official languages, English and French. The law says the federal government must serve you in either one, anywhere in the country.
text.fr: Le Canada a deux langues officielles, l'anglais et le français. La loi oblige le gouvernement fédéral à vous servir dans l'une ou l'autre, partout au pays.

source.quote: English and French define the reality of day-to-day life for most people and are the country’s official languages. The federal government is required by law to provide services throughout Canada in English and French.

verification.evidence: English and French define the reality of day-to-day life for most people and are the country’s official languages. The federal government is required by law to provide services throughout Canada in English and French.

text.en: Just one province has both of them as its own official languages. That province is New Brunswick.
text.fr: Une seule province a les deux comme langues officielles. Cette province, c'est le Nouveau-Brunswick.

source.quote: New Brunswick is the only officially bilingual province.

verification.evidence: While the majority of Francophones live in the province of Quebec, one million Francophones live in Ontario, New Brunswick and Manitoba, with a smaller presence in other provinces. New Brunswick is the only officially bilingual province.

text.en: Three questions follow, about who Canadians are. Take as long as you need.
text.fr: Trois questions suivent, sur qui sont les Canadiens. Prenez tout le temps qu'il vous faut.
